nodes.name: Every Five Minutes
nodes.notes: Five minutes is the rhythm's resolution, and SC-001 is written against it: each touch arrives within five minutes of the member's chosen time. n8n holds no schedule beyond this pulse -- constitution II -- because a member in Cairo and one in Berlin both want 22:00 and it is not the same instant, so a cron that knew the times would need one entry per zone. The gateway decides whose time it is.

nodes.name: Run Now
nodes.notes:
The admin portal's Run button. It reaches /internal/rhythm/prompt, not the tick, and the difference matters: the tick is conditional and idempotent per local date, so pressing Run on it would do nothing once the evening had already fired -- which looks exactly like a broken button. The prompt endpoint is unconditional and ignores the claim, which is what an operator asking 'does this work' actually wants.

Body: { userId?, kind: 'plan' | 'end_of_day' | 'morning' }. Omitting userId reaches every member, so it is the one call here that is not safe to press twice out of curiosity.

nodes.name: Tick
nodes.notes:
Three tries, five seconds apart. Retrying is safe because every touch claims its local date before it sends: a retry after a timeout finds the date claimed and sends nothing, so the worst a retry costs is a wasted pass.

Ten minutes of timeout, not two. A firing tick builds a draft per due member, and from P8 that includes a meal line from the local model -- which measured 39 seconds to first token on a cold load. A two-minute ceiling would abort the evening of whoever happened to be late in the page.

`neverError` is off deliberately. A 401 between n8n and the gateway has to FAIL here so the error workflow fires and the heartbeat goes stale; exactly that silent 401 once went unnoticed for days, which is why every job writes an ops_heartbeats row and /health calls it stale after fifteen minutes.

nodes.name: Prompt Now
nodes.notes:
No retry, and that is the one place this workflow differs from the sweep. The prompt endpoint is unconditional by design, so a retry after a timeout would send a second copy of a touch the first attempt may well have delivered. An operator pressing Run again is a decision; a retry loop doing it for them is not.

The body is forwarded verbatim from the webhook so the portal chooses the member and the kind.

nodes.name: Counts
nodes.notes: The counts are the execution's output, so n8n's own log is the record of what each pass did. `contracts/internal.md` fixes this shape: { users, planPrompts, endOfDay, morning, checkins, ms }. A bare acknowledgement would make 'ran and nobody was due' and 'ran and sent four hundred briefings' the same line -- and this log is all anybody has when asking why a member's 22:00 summary did not arrive.
